name.text: CHEM_U04_L01_QZ Q01 - Evidence of Chemical Reactions

questiontext.text:
MLA Standard: MLA.CHEM.REA.01; MLA.CHEM.MAT.02

Stimulus:

ScenarioObservationEvidence type
Two clear liquids become cloudysolid appearsprecipitate/new substance
Water boilsbubbles formphysical phase change unless new substance evidence appears

Question: Which answer avoids the common misconception?

generalfeedback.text: Use the embedded reaction evidence, equation, data table, or model before choosing an answer.

answer.text: Bubbles alone are not enough because boiling can also produce bubbles.

feedback.text: Correct. For MLA.CHEM.REA.01; MLA.CHEM.MAT.02, 'Bubbles alone are not enough because boiling can also produce bubbles.' is the strongest answer because it uses reaction evidence, equations, conservation, or stoichiometric reasoning from the stimulus or question. It matches the evidence in this item instead of relying on a vague claim.
